transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. As part of the normal policy review for the analytics backfill cluster, I need to confirm operational requirements from each of your areas before I give final approval. The current draft policy has 12 baseline workers, scales out at 80 percent utilization, permits spot instances, sets an $18,000 monthly spending cap, uses the shared compute pool, and retains audit records for 30 days. Could data platform, FinOps, and security and compliance each confirm whether this draft meets your requirements, or flag any changes you need?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag two compliance requirements for this policy. While reviewing dataset classifications for a separate audit, I confirmed that regulated exports processed by this cluster must run in a dedicated compute pool, not the shared compute pool. Additionally, audit records must be retained for exactly 180 days, not 30 days. I have not yet opened the compliance ticket for this policy, but these changes are required before approval.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag two FinOps requirements for this policy. During this month's invoice reconciliation, I confirmed that the cluster's reserved-capacity credits expire this quarter, so spot capacity is not approved for these jobs and the correct monthly spending cap is exactly $14,000, not $18,000. I have not yet posted the reconciliation note in the infrastructure review thread, but these changes are required before approval.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag two data platform requirements for this policy. While checking an unrelated dashboard query this morning, I measured the backfill's overnight queue behavior and confirmed that it needs exactly 18 baseline workers and a scale-out trigger at exactly 70 percent utilization to finish before the 06:00 UTC reporting run. I have not updated the policy draft yet, but these changes are required before approval.
transcript.speaker: A2
